meta.title: Media Delivery: Database Path vs Direct Storage Path

views.label: A: media inside the database
views.note: Every uncached view pushes the whole file through the app and database.

views.label: B: direct storage (TPS design)
views.note: Files come from Cloudflare's cache; R2 is read only on a miss. The TPS app is not involved.

components.label: Application
components.explanation: Fully buffering a 2 MB image means 100 simultaneous requests hold about 200 MB in one instance (illustrative; streaming changes this). Large media competes with business requests for memory, CPU and connections.

components.label: Database
components.explanation: BYTEA is a valid choice for small transactional binary records, such as a 2 KB signature. For large media, each uncached read adds SQL processing, protocol serialization, possible decompression, encryption, network transfer and storage I/O, and backups and exports grow.

components.label: Cloudflare CDN
components.explanation: Serves cached copies close to the visitor. Only a cache miss is fetched from R2.

components.label: Photo + video storage
components.explanation: Object storage for the 170.15 MB library. Public media is read directly; private files would still need authorization and signed URLs. If PostgreSQL is used, it can store each file's metadata and R2 object key. R2 and the database need their own backup and consistency policies.

boundaries.label: A · Media stored in the database (uncached)
B · Direct object storage (TPS launch design)

cards.title: When the database is right
items: Small transactional binary records (a 2 KB record vs a 2 MB image is 1,000× the payload)
Media metadata and R2 object keys

cards.title: Cost of path A per uncached view
items: SQL, serialization, buffering, encryption, transfer, storage I/O
